paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus doesn't just have a resurrection, He IS the resurrection. Martha knew Lazarus would rise "in the resurrection at the last day," and she had that one filed away neatly. Then Jesus says, "I am the resurrection and the life" (John 11:24-25). He moves the whole thing out of a calendar and puts it in a Person standing right in front of her.

Now look at what Jesus does with the sisters' grief. Martha says, "Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died," and Mary says the exact same thing (John 11:21, 32). He doesn't scold either one, and at the tomb it says, "Jesus wept" (John 11:35). I think that tells you your hurt is not a bother to Him. And He doesn't stop at tears, either. He asks Martha, "Do you believe this?" (John 11:26), and He calls her to see "the glory of God" (John 11:40).

So what do you do with that, baker? You bring Him the honest stuff, the "if You had been here" stuff, and you believe Him, because He promises, "Whoever believes in Me will live, even though he dies" (John 11:25), which means death doesn't get the last word on anyone who trusts Him. Believing doesn't mean you have it all figured out, since Martha still said "by now he stinks" (John 11:39), and Jesus kept right on working. And when He calls, "Lazarus, come out!" (John 11:43), the dead man comes out, so I'm keeping my ovens hot, and this story isn't over yet, friend.
